trinity: Trinity College and the Book of Kells

Ireland's oldest university, founded in 1592, with stone squares and the Campanile. In the Old Library you see the Book of Kells, the 9th-century illuminated manuscript of the four Gospels, and the long book-lined hall, the Long Room.
guinness: The museum of Ireland's most famous beer, in an old 1904 fermentation building shaped like a giant pint glass: seven floors on how Guinness is made, with a pint included in the ticket, to drink in the panoramic bar on the top floor.
kilmainham: The former prison where the leaders of the 1916 Rising were held and executed: a key place in the history of Irish independence. You see the top-lit Victorian wing, the cells and the execution yard.
christ: Dublin's medieval cathedral, founded by the Vikings in the 11th century and rebuilt in stone by the Normans. The oldest part is the crypt, the longest in Ireland, with silver treasures and "Tom" the mummified cat with the mouse.
patrick: Ireland's largest cathedral, on the spot where, tradition says, St Patrick baptised the first Christians. Jonathan Swift, author of "Gulliver's Travels", who was dean of the cathedral, is buried here.
temple: The district of cobbled lanes on the south bank of the Liffey, with colourful pubs and live music. Next to it, the Ha'penny Bridge, the 1816 cast-iron footbridge, is the symbol of Dublin.
grafton: Grafton Street and St Stephen's Green

The pedestrian shopping street, full of street performers, leading to the great Victorian park of St Stephen's Green with its pond, little bridges and ducks. Along the street is the statue of Molly Malone.
archaeo: The museum of Irish treasures: Bronze Age gold, the Ardagh Chalice and the Tara Brooch, and the "bog bodies", Iron Age men preserved by peat for 2,000 years.
merrion: The national gallery, with Caravaggio, Vermeer and Goya and a large room devoted to Irish painters, a short walk from Merrion Square: the Georgian square with colourful front doors and the statue of Oscar Wilde lounging on a rock.
epic: The interactive museum telling the story of ten million Irish emigrants around the world, in an underground warehouse in the Docklands. More engaging than a traditional museum: you listen, touch and can even look up your own surname.
phoenix: One of Europe's largest enclosed city parks, about an hour's walk from the centre. Hundreds of fallow deer live here, and inside are Dublin Zoo, the Wellington Monument (the tallest obelisk in Europe) and the residence of the Irish President.
